sources.title: CLIA; Virtual Access, Gynecologic Cytology PT, Personnel Qualifications, and Other Changes (proposed rule)

status_summary: CMS and CDC issued a request for information on CLIA regulations on 2026-07-16 (comments closed 2026-09-14) and a proposed rule on 2026-10-08 (CMS-3478-P, 91 FR 64480, comments due 2026-12-07). The proposal would loosen laboratory director qualifications (one year of experience or 20 hours of continuing education as alternatives, no board certification for doctoral directors, residency or fellowship laboratory training counted), drop human-only limits on qualifying research and laboratory science background, add virtual access to digital data and digital gynecologic cytology proficiency testing, and remove SARS-CoV-2 reporting requirements. The preamble records commenter concerns about scope limits on animal-science and histology staff and notes that some laboratories employ nonclinical scientists, but it does not propose a separate CLIA certification equivalency pathway for non-clinical laboratories or revise scope of practice as such.
